intended_object: The functorial action on the W-type of a multivariate polynomial functor P of arity n+1: a map of type vectors g : α ⟹ β induces a map W_P(α) → W_P(β). This comes from the docstring "W-types are functorial".
explanation: The definition is simply `g <$$> x`. This uses the `MvFunctor` instance on `P.W` (`P.W α = P.wp.Obj α`). That map leaves the tree shape unchanged and post-composes the labels on paths with g. The lemma `w_map_wMk` that follows confirms the expected recursive behaviour: g <$$> wMk a f' f = wMk a (g ⊚ f') (fun i => g <$$> f i). That is exactly how a W-type acts as a functor in its first n parameters. This is the usual construction, stated at its natural generality: an arbitrary multivariate polynomial functor and arbitrary type vectors. It is a named wrapper around Mathlib's general `MvFunctor.map`, so it adds no restriction.
